defect: _headings_from_plain() turns a short line into a heading even when the next paragraph is another short line, so it becomes a heading with no body; split() then replaces it with the next sibling heading and drops the empty section. The text is silently lost from the brain. Every plug-in reader goes through this path (.docx, .rtf, .xlsx, .pptx, .html, .csv, .eml): a Word memo with four short lines loses 'Revenue up' entirely.

repro.cmd:
python3 -c "
import zipfile
lines = ['Quarterly kickoff', 'Revenue up', 'Hiring plan', 'Ship readers by Friday.']
body = ''.join('<w:p><w:r><w:t>%s</w:t></w:r></w:p>' % s for s in lines)
with zipfile.ZipFile('heuristic-loss.docx', 'w') as z:
    z.writestr('word/document.xml', '<w:document xmlns:w=\"http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main\"><w:body>' + body + '</w:body></w:document>')
from ingest import chunk
d = chunk.load('heuristic-loss.docx', source='repro', default_scope='internal')
text = '\n'.join(c.content for c in d.chunks)
missing = [s for s in lines if s not in text]
assert not missing, 'lost from the brain: %s' % missing
print('all lines kept')
"

evidence.notes: Builds a four-paragraph .docx in the work dir and loads it through chunk.load() exactly as intake does; asserts every line survives into some chunk. At the pinned commit: AssertionError: lost from the brain: ['Revenue up']. Found by the readers goal: the .pptx builder (CompuBrain #26) noticed body text disappearing and worked around it in its own reader instead of fixing chunk.py, which was outside its scope. Fix belongs in ingest/chunk.py; a heading with no body must keep its text (as a body line or in the trail of a chunk), and the existing ingest tests and goals/readers/acceptance.sh must stay green.
